newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: Anglo gold mines profits dip in latest quarter.
newsitem.headline: Anglo gold mines profits dip in latest quarter.

text.p: The world's biggest gold producer, Anglo American Corp of South Africa Ltd, on Thursday reported lower profits from its gold mines for the September quarter, with profit down three percent to 312.3 million rand ($68.5 million) from 322.7 million in the June quarter.
Anglo's gold and uranium division, Anglogold, said the fall in profit could be attributed to annual wage increases and higher working costs at some of the company's mines.

"This September quarter, as with every September quarter, is the quarter in which we accommodate the full impact of the wage increases," Anglogold chairman Bobby Godsell said at the results presentation.
The five mines in the Anglogold stable produced 52,437 kg of gold in the three months to end-September, slightly down from 52,631 kg produced in the June quarter.
But the company said it received a four percent higher price per kg of gold sold.
Anglogold said it received an average revenue of 54,919 rand/kg against 52,867 rand/kg in the preceding quarter.
Unit working costs increased by six percent to 43,044 rand/kg from 40,592 rand/kg in the June quarter.

Godsell attributed the hike in working costs to the higher wage bill and lower gold production at the world's largest gold mine, Free State Consolidated Gold Mines Ltd (Freegold) and Western Deep Levels Ltd.
Capital expenditure was higher at 199.3 million rand from 180 million rand in the June quarter.

"If you look at the important sources of that increase, at Western Deep Levels we've seen a six million rand increase. This is part of the funding of the south (shaft) deepening process and will continue for a number of years," Godsell said.
Other major capital spending projects were at East Rand Gold and Uranium Company (Ergo)and Elandsrand Gold Mining Company.
The star performer in Anglogold's stable in the September quarter was Ergo. The company lifted attributable profit by 23 percent to 18.4 million rand from 14.9 million in the previous quarter.
Elandsrand also turned in another strong performance as the mine lifted available profit by 19 percent to 39.1 million rand from 32.8 million in the previous quarter.
Elandsrand increased gold production to 4,209 kg from 3,973 kg in the June quarter and Anglogold said this was mainly due to an increase in yield.
The average yield at Elandsrand increased to 7.99 grammes/t from 7.32 g/t in the June quarter.
Freegold increased available profit to 129.5 million rand from 126.5 million rand in the previous quarter, but gold production dropped by four percent to 20,381 kg from 21,261 kg.
Anglogold said the reduced gold production reflected planned downsizing from the closure of Freddies No.9 shaft and rationalisation of Western Holdings No.5 shaft.
Freegold's working costs increased by five percent to 955.7 million rand. Anglogold expected capital expenditure at the mine to be 92 million rand in the nine months to December.
Western Deep Levels reported a 30 percent drop in available profit for the September quarter to 32.5 million rand from 46.5 million in the three months to end-June. ($1=4.5565 Rand)
